answer: Divergent History Challenge. Each identity must maintain a private, append-only event log; peers challenge it with fresh random checkpoints. A clone shares history until it diverges, so any divergence yields contradictory signed branches that a beacon timestamped earlier exposes. To pass, an attacker must run a separate consistent log per clone, paying full storage, signing, and synchronization costs per identity. The mechanism forms a bridge between challenge and evidence while the common basalt ledger anchors dispute outcomes.
